sections.title: The two most irregular verbs, made past
sections.content: eszik ("eat") and iszik ("drink") are the most irregular verbs you've met, and the past tense keeps that up: their indefinite stems are evett- and ivott-, not a simple ett-/itt- pattern you could have guessed. Learn these stems directly — and remember the definite vs indefinite rule from the last lesson still applies on top of them.

items.english: I ate a lot of fruit yesterday.
I drank a glass of water.

sections.content: Only 3rd person singular indefinite really surprises you here: evett, not "ett", and ivott, not "itt". Every other person follows the ett-/itt- stem you'd expect from ettem/ittam. The definite forms — ette, itta — go back to the plain stem, same pattern as olvasta from the last lesson.
